How we work.

How this hub decides, how a change travels, who signs off on an asset, the one checklist before anything is published, and one way to name, file and archive everything. Short enough to follow on a busy day.

How this hub worksTwo change pathsWho approvesThe asset flowChecklistFeedback labelsFile namingVersionsFoldersFigma filesArchiveOpen items
Current

The authority order, the two change paths, the approval matrix and flow, the checklist, file naming, folders and the archive are decided (R-01, R-02, R-121 to R-127, U-30). Legal approves every social post at launch (R-122); files live in a Google Shared Drive and approved files move to the approved folder with the name unchanged (R-124); the approval log is a sheet in that Drive (R-125).

To confirm

Who the clinical, legal and operations approvers are, who approves medical content, the turnaround per step and the website backlog tool (O-17 and the open items below). The roles below are functions, not people, until then. See Open items.

How this hub works.

One order, used on every page, in every file and in every review. When two sources disagree, the higher step wins.

  1. Decided rules and tokens win.

    Every rule, decision, exception and open item lives in the rulebook (brand-rules.md); every value lives in tokens/tokens.json, and brand.css is generated from it (R-01, R-03).

  2. The rulebook wins on wording and compliance.

    The hub pages explain and mirror the rules and never add a rule of their own. A process decision gets a number in the rulebook before a page shows it (R-02, R-121 to R-129).

  3. The designer's Figma covers only what is not decided yet.

    The website and logo files are the source for anything no rule or token covers. They are read and exported, never changed (R-01).

  4. Our own Figma files follow the rules.

    Our three files, unifiedmeds · Design System, unifiedmeds · Website and unifiedmeds · Assessment, are updated whenever a rule or a value changes (R-01). See Figma files.

  5. A clinical or legal no stops it.

    Brand cannot overrule a clinical or legal no on any asset. Clinical and legal ask for a change; brand makes it in the brand's own way (R-121).

Two change paths.

A rule or a value changes on one path; a finished asset is approved on the other (R-123). They meet only when an asset needs a rule that does not exist yet: then the rule path runs first.

1 · A rule or a value changes.

A rule changes in this order: decision → brand-rules.md → tokens → changelog → release. No silent mismatches. Exceptions are logged before they ship. Open items are marked To confirm. A change to palette, type scale, layout or a rule's meaning opens a new edition.R-78 to R-83
  1. Decision. Avi decides. The decision gets a U-number and a date in the rulebook's decision log.
  2. Rulebook. The rule text changes in brand-rules.md; tools/build_rulebook.py regenerates the rulebook page.
  3. Tokens. tokens/tokens.json changes; tools/build_tokens.py regenerates brand.css.
  4. Changelog. One entry: the date, the decision and rule IDs, the tokens that changed and the pages affected.
  5. Release. The pages are rebuilt (tools/build_pages.py), tools/check.py prints 0 problems, our Figma files are brought in line, and the site is uploaded.

2 · An asset is approved.

Every website page, landing page, ad, post, email, label and video takes the same seven steps before it goes out: who approves what, then the flow (R-121, R-123). The asset is checked against the rules in force; it never changes a rule on its own.

  1. Draft from the hub templates, named by the convention.
  2. Brand check against the checklist.
  3. Clinical, only with medical content.
  4. Legal: claims, offers, consent and required lines.
  5. Final sign-off by Brand on the exact file that ships.
  6. Publish from the approved folder, unchanged.
  7. Log: one row in the approval log.

Mobile · 390. The two paths stack: the rule path first, then the asset path.

The asset flow.

Seven steps, in this order (R-121, R-123). A step with a dashed circle runs only when the asset needs it; the table below says when.

  1. DraftMaker

    Built from the hub templates, named by the convention, saved in work.

  2. Brand checkAvi or a delegate

    Runs the brand part of the checklist. Fixes come back to the maker.

  3. ClinicalClinical team

    Only with medical content. Checks every medical line and the safety text.

  4. LegalLegal and compliance

    Checks claims, offers, consent and required lines.

  5. Final sign-offBrand (Avi)

    Looks at the exact file that ships, after every change.

  6. PublishOwner of the channel

    Ships the approved file, unchanged, from the approved folder.

  7. LogOwner of the channel

    One row in the approval log: file, version, who approved, where it went.

The pre-publish checklist.

One checklist for every asset (R-123). Run it on the exact file that ships and write the codes you checked in the approval log. Brand, Compliance, Accessibility, Discretion, Tracking and Filing apply to everything; the Dev block applies to website and product builds. Every page and screen is checked at 1440 and 390 wide at least; website builds also at 768 and 1024 (R-27, R-107).

Download the checklistDownload the naming guide

Brand

  1. B1The name is "unifiedmeds", lower case; the former brand name appears nowhere (R-07, U-16).
  2. B2Colours come from the tokens; Yellow once per view at most, never a background (R-03, R-11).
  3. B3DM Serif Display and Inter only; serif never below 24 desktop or 21 mobile (R-18, R-21).
  4. B4Buttons are rounded rectangles, radius 5, never pills; two buttons side by side never share a colour (R-40, R-112).
  5. B5Logo from the exported files, the right version for the ground, clear space and minimum sizes kept (R-91, R-92, R-118).
  6. B6Sentence case; headlines end with a full stop and are never questions; no em or en dashes (R-24).
  7. B7Cards in a row share one height and one action line (R-98).
  8. B8Two shapes per surface at most; every capsule keeps its divider (R-106, R-109).

Compliance

  1. C1No benefit claim, price or symptom list in a hero (R-58, R-61).
  2. C2Prescription names only where safety information sits; never in heroes, ads, social assets or captions (R-65, R-108).
  3. C3"Assessment only. Not a diagnosis." next to every assessment button above the fold and on every assessment screen (R-63).
  4. C4A licensed provider is named for every next step (R-64).
  5. C5No statistics, reviews, testimonials, ratings or promised times; a demo review shows DEMO ONLY and "Member · age", never "Verified" (R-67, R-68).
  6. C6Illustrative medical content shows DEMO ONLY; items marked Legal review required stay off (R-69, R-87).
  7. C7Footer reads "© 2026 unifiedmeds"; marketing email has unsubscribe and address (R-88).
  8. C8Open placeholders stay visible until they are decided: "[charge line · operations]" and "[about N minutes · O-12]" (R-62, O-12).

Accessibility

  1. A1Text passes WCAG AA contrast (R-72).
  2. A2Every image has alt text; on web pages text is live, never inside an image.
  3. A3Tap targets 44 by 44 or larger; focus ring visible (R-73, R-74).
  4. A4Checked at 1440 and 390 wide: nothing cut, no sideways scroll (R-77, R-107).
  5. A5With reduced motion, nothing moves (R-76).
  6. A6Video has captions; nothing flashes.

Discretion

  1. D1Subject lines, previews, notifications and sender names never name a condition or a medicine (R-108).
  2. D2No health data in any email.
  3. D3File names and image addresses inside emails are neutral (category all).
  4. D4No ad audience built from health data or from the assessment.

Tracking

  1. T1No tracking pixels, ad tags or session replay on condition or product pages (R-71).
  2. T2Assessment answers only on the clinical intake domain (R-70).
  3. T3No analytics before consent, the assessment included, unless legal approves an exception (U-31).
  4. T4Buttons carry data-cta named by position; links carry the UTM pattern.
  5. T5No name, email, ID or condition in any URL or UTM value.

Filing

  1. F1The file is named by the convention; no "final" in any name (R-126).
  2. F2The approved version sits in the approved folder, unchanged (R-124).
  3. F3The log has its row; the version it replaces moved to the archive (R-125, R-127).

Dev · website and product builds

  1. Dev1python3 -I tools/check.py prints 0 problems: no colour literal in styling, only DM Serif Display and Inter, no broken links (R-03, R-83).
  2. Dev2Checked at 1440 and 390 always, and at 768 and 1024 for website builds (R-27, R-107).
  3. Dev3Every value comes from a token; nothing is built without one, and brand.css is never edited by hand (R-03).
  4. Dev4Only logged exceptions differ: E-02 header button 44px, E-03 mobile menu bar button 48px, E-04 the price in the checkout card, E-05 the inline "state not served" message on screen 01 with Continue disabled.
  5. Dev5Focus: tab through every page; a 2px Deep Teal ring at a 3px offset, Paper on dark grounds and photos, never hidden (R-73).
  6. Dev6Keyboard and touch: nothing works on hover only; the menu opens with Enter or ↓, Esc closes it and returns focus, aria-expanded updates (R-75, R-46).
  7. Dev7Reduced motion emulated: every state is instant. With motion on, nothing loops except the loader (R-76, R-53).
  8. Dev8No link to a retired Figma file, to an archived page as if current, or to a Phase 2 category before it launches (R-04, R-06).
  9. Dev9No watermarked or stand-in photo ships; meaningful images have alt text, decorative images an empty alt (R-39).

Feedback labels.

Start every review comment with one label. The label decides where it goes and who acts. Developers find the same four on the developer handoff.

LabelUse it whenWhere it goesWhat happens
BUGThe build does not match the rules, the tokens or our Figma files.The website backlog, with the page, the width, the Figma node and the rule ID.The developer fixes the code. No rule or token changes.
CHANGESomeone wants a value or a rule to be different.A proposed decision for Avi in the decision log.Build to the current rule until Avi decides. If approved, it takes change path 1.
ADOPTSomething built works better than the spec and should become the rule.A proposed decision for Avi in the decision log, with a link to the built example.If approved, it takes change path 1 and our Figma files follow. Until then it is not the rule.
QUESTIONThe spec is missing or unclear, or two sources disagree.Open items in the rulebook (the O-list), with one owner.The owner answers. Keep building everything the question does not block.

Where the convention applies.

The shared drive, every export, and every file sent to someone outside the team.

Where it does not.

Code and this hub keep their own short names (assets/email/shipping.html); their history lives in the repository, not in the name.

Mobile · 390. The pattern wraps field by field; the long example names break anywhere instead of pushing the page sideways.

Versions and the approved state.

Status lives in the folder, not in the name (R-124, R-126, U-30).

A new number for every shared change.

v01 is the first version anyone else sees. Every change that is shared again is the next number. Saves between shares keep the same number.

Approved files move, they are not renamed.

On approval the file moves from 1-work to 3-approved with its name unchanged, and the log records who approved it and when.

Why a folder, not a suffix.

A renamed file breaks every link and every log line that points to it, and a suffix invites "approved-2". A folder shows status at a glance, in one place.

Never edit an approved file.

A change starts the next version in work. When that version is approved, the old one moves to the archive.

Folders on the shared drive.

A Google Shared Drive, so files belong to the company, not to one person (R-124, U-30). The approval log is a sheet in 00-admin (R-125). One folder per channel, numbered so the order never changes, and the same four stages inside each.

Figma files.

Our three files sit in one Figma project, unifiedmeds, under fixed names that never change: no edition number and no "Copy" in a name. The edition lives in each file's version history (saved as "Edition 04 · 19.11.2026") and in the Changelog. Website and Assessment take their components from the Design System file. The designer's files are read and exported, never changed. Opening a file needs access to the team project.

FileOpenRoleAccess

The separator is " · ".

A space, a middle dot, a space, as in every page and frame of our files. Never a dash. Every desktop frame has its mobile twin, named with "Mobile" as the variant.

No status or version in a Figma name.

No "final", "v2", "new" or "copy". Status goes in a tag inside the frame; Figma keeps its own version history.

Archive, never delete.

Earlier editions, replaced files and removed pages are kept, outside anything published as current (R-127, R-04, U-16).

Move, with the name unchanged.

A replaced or retired file moves to 9-archive in its channel folder; a whole retired edition moves to 99-archive. In this hub, a page or file that leaves moves to archive/ with its path kept.

Log the move.

The approval log row gets "archived, replaced by" and the new file name; a hub move gets a changelog line.

Never linked as current.

Nothing in the archive is linked from a live page, the hub menu or a template. Emptying the trash is Avi's call only.
